overview: Mongolia is a landlocked country in East Asia, between Russia and China. Its capital, Ulaanbaatar, is home to almost half of the population and is the coldest capital city in the world. In the 1200s Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire, which became the largest connected land empire in history. Many Mongolians still herd animals and live in traditional round tents called gers.

geography.text: Mongolia is one of the most thinly populated countries in the world. The north and west have mountains, forests and lakes, the centre and east are vast grassy steppes, and the south is the Gobi Desert, where many dinosaur fossils have been found. Winters are long and bitterly cold.

history.text: In 1206 Genghis Khan united the Mongol tribes and began building the largest connected land empire in history, which stretched from Korea to eastern Europe. After the empire broke up, Mongolia later came under China's Qing dynasty. It declared independence in 1911 and became a communist state allied with the Soviet Union in 1924. A peaceful revolution in 1990 brought democracy.

events.title: Yuan dynasty
events.text: Kublai Khan founds a Mongol dynasty to rule China.

events.title: Qing rule
events.text: Mongolia comes under the Qing dynasty.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Mongolia declares independence as the Qing collapse.

events.title: People's Republic
events.text: A communist state is founded with Soviet support.

government.text: Mongolia is a parliamentary republic and has been a democracy since 1990. The State Great Khural, its parliament, chooses the Prime Minister, and the President is elected directly for a single six-year term.

economy.text: Mining dominates Mongolia's economy: it exports coal, copper and gold, mostly to China. Herding is still a way of life for many families, and Mongolia has far more livestock than people.

culture.text: Mongolia is the most sparsely populated country in the world. Around a quarter of the people still live as nomadic herders in round felt tents called gers. Throat singing, known as khöömei, produces two notes at once and is listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Gers
items.text: Portable round tents of felt and wood.

items.title: Khöömei
items.text: Throat singing that makes two notes at once.

items.title: Genghis Khan statue
items.text: A 40-metre steel statue of the founder of the Mongol Empire.

sport.text: The Naadam festival every July features the 'three games of men': wrestling, horse racing and archery, though women now compete in archery and racing. Mongolian wrestlers have dominated Japanese sumo for decades.

items.title: Naadam
items.text: Festival of wrestling, horse racing and archery.

items.title: Sumo
items.text: Many grand champions of Japanese sumo have been Mongolian.
